title: Tottenham Hotspur — Premier League club content (2026/27)
source: FICTIONAL. Written by the REROUTE team for the hackathon demo, modelled on common football club-content practice: club-owned social channels, a home-market window for full-match recordings, no match broadcast footage in advertising, a club group image-rights pool, partner exclusivity and stadium conditions of entry. No Tottenham Hotspur, Premier League, player or sponsor agreement was supplied or consulted.
disclaimer: FICTIONAL DEMO POLICY — not an actual club, league, player or sponsor agreement. DEMO POLICY — NOT VERIFIED LEGAL CLEARANCE.

provenance.description: Club-produced footage filed in the club's ScorePlay workspace and tagged "partner content"

rules.explanation: Premier League footage of the 2026/27 season is covered by the club's content licence.
The licence covers the club's own accounts on Instagram, Facebook, X, TikTok and YouTube only.
Club content may be targeted at the licensed territories GB, IE, US, CA, AU and NZ. Other markets are held by international media partners.
Full-match recordings come from the live broadcast feed and may only be shown in the home market (GB, IE).
Club content may be used for editorial, organic, sponsored-partner and commercial club posts, subject to the people and brand rules.
Match broadcast footage (highlights and full-match recordings) may not be used to sell merchandise or tickets. It is licensed for editorial and club-social use only.
The licence runs for the 2026/27 season, from 1 Jul 2026 to 30 Jun 2027.
Players, staff and spectators who appear in match-day coverage may be shown in editorial and organic club posts.

The club image-rights pool covers sponsored and commercial use of first-team squad members and staff. It applies only when ScorePlay registers the person in the Tottenham Hotspur squad. Opponents and unverified people are not covered.
Under the stadium conditions of entry, crowd and stadium shots may be used commercially. This applies when ScorePlay lists no player and video analysis finds no identifiable player.
Kit branding and stadium signage that appear incidentally may be shown in editorial and organic club posts.
Sponsored and commercial club posts may show the club's own marks and its listed official partners: AIA and Nike.
Sponsored and commercial club posts may not show third-party brands (for example opponent kit sponsors or stadium boards) because official partners have exclusivity.
